# Instructions

Implement a RESTful API for tracking IOUs.

Four roommates have a habit of borrowing money from each other frequently, and have trouble remembering who owes whom, and how much.

Your task is to implement a simple [RESTful API][restful-wikipedia] that receives [IOU][iou]s as POST requests, and can deliver specified summary information via GET requests.

## API Specification

### User object

```json
{
  "name": "Adam",
  "owes": {
    "Bob": 12.0,
    "Chuck": 4.0,
    "Dan": 9.5
  },
  "owed_by": {
    "Bob": 6.5,
    "Dan": 2.75
  },
  "balance": "<(total owed by other users) - (total owed to other users)>"
}
```

### Methods

| Description              | HTTP Method | URL    | Payload Format                                                            | Response w/o Payload                   | Response w/ Payload                                                             |
| ------------------------ | ----------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| List of user information | GET         | /users | `{"users":["Adam","Bob"]}`                                                | `{"users":<List of all User objects>}` | `{"users":<List of User objects for <users> (sorted by name)}`                  |
| Create user              | POST        | /add   | `{"user":<name of new user (unique)>}`                                    | N/A                                    | `<User object for new user>`                                                    |
| Create IOU               | POST        | /iou   | `{"lender":<name of lender>,"borrower":<name of borrower>,"amount":5.25}` | N/A                                    | `{"users":<updated User objects for <lender> and <borrower> (sorted by name)>}` |

## Other Resources

- [REST API Tutorial][restfulapi]
- Example RESTful APIs
  - [GitHub][github-rest]
  - [Reddit][reddit-rest]

[restful-wikipedia]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer
[iou]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOU
[github-rest]: https://developer.github.com/v3/
[reddit-rest]: https://web.archive.org/web/20231202231149/https://www.reddit.com/dev/api/
[restfulapi]: https://restfulapi.net/

Use the instructions above to complete `rest_api.py`. Keep the existing function and class names: tests you cannot see import them. Use only the Python standard library.

{"summary": "`RestAPI` in `rest_api.py` now handles all three endpoints, using only the standard library and keeping the original class and method names. Payloads come in as JSON strings and responses go out as JSON strings.

- **`GET /users`**: returns every user sorted by name. If the payload lists names in `users`, it returns only those users.
- **`POST /add`**: creates a user with empty `owes` and `owed_by` and returns the new user object. A duplicate name raises a `ValueError`.
- **`POST /iou`**: records the loan and returns the lender and borrower sorted by name. Debts between the two are offset against each other, so if the lender already owed the borrower, that amount goes down first. A debt that reaches zero is removed, and if the new loan is larger than the old debt, the direction flips. `balance` is always worked out fresh as (total owed by others) − (total owed to others).
- **Errors**: an unknown URL or user, or lending to yourself, raises a `ValueError`.

There are no test files in the project, so I checked it by running a short script against the class. It covered a partly offsetting IOU, one that cancels the debt exactly, one that flips the debt's direction, adding a user, and both forms of `GET /users`. All the outputs matched the spec. The hidden tests haven't been run.", "outputs": ["rest_api.py"]}
